name: the_width_mate_centres_the_tab
why: REPORT 8CD843, ROUND 21, POINT 7 (28/10/2026). The owner's rule 2 for 26M000002 is «centre with width»: he mated 4 components by hand with a width mate, and the bridge could read it (N63) but not make it. Now «mate» takes «width»: two faces of the width on component_a («face_a», «face_a2»), two faces of the tab on component_b («face_b», «face_b2»), and the tab goes in the middle of the width (swMateWidth_Centered).
defect_caught: The width and the tab swapped (the marks 1 and 16 of IAssemblyDoc~AddMate5.html given the other way round), a width mate made off centre, a mate that SOLIDWORKS answers without placing the tab, and a width mate asked with one face per component taken as another mate.
_why_these_numbers: The base of «the_state_reads_how_a_mate_is_set», 120 x 80 x 10 mm centred on the origin: its left and right faces at x -60 and +60 mm, the middle at x 0. The clip 40 x 20 x 4 mm starts at x 30 mm, 30 mm off the middle; centred, its origin goes to x 0. The coincident mate first puts it on the base (y 10 mm), so that the width mate moves it along x only.

expect.why: the clip lies on the base: the width mate below moves it along x only
the width mate is there, counted on both components

expect.tolerance_why: THE TAB IN THE MIDDLE OF THE WIDTH: the clip started at x 30 mm, centred between x -60 and +60 its origin is at x 0; y 10 mm from the coincident mate, z unchanged

expect.why: the two faces of the width, said as they were asked
the two faces of the tab
read back from the tree: IMate2.Type gives swMateWIDTH

message_includes: A «width» mate wants two faces on each component
«face_a2» and «face_b2» are only for a «width» mate
